articles.title: Shah launches India's first counter-terrorism policy | Daily Pioneer
articles.content: September 29, 2026 Shah launches India’s first counter-terrorism policy Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pramod Kumar Singh Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah on Monday inaugurated the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR-CT Policy and Strategy’ in New Delhi. The meeting brought together senior security and police officials to review and implement India’s first national counter-terrorism doctrine. Shah said the Government of India, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has adopted a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism. He called for ongoing review of the PRAHAAR framework based on analysis of terror incidents, and for building a mechanism that can serve the country over the next decade. He said the principles of PRAHAAR must be implemented at the police station level, and that all levels of the security system should act proactively. Shah called for an automated counter-terrorism response at every level to avoid delays and ensure effective action. He said central agencies, state police, and other stakeholders must coordinate closely so that there is no delay when a threat arises. The Home Minister said the Government has already used this coordinated approach in recent operations. Between 2019 and 2026, authorities brought back 288 fugitive criminals from 36 countries. Improved coordination led to the dismantling of over 40 modules of the Shahzad Bhatti network, which was involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives, and narcotics. Authorities registered more than 100 FIRs and arrested 350 people across 15 States. The network has been declared a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. Shah also launched a new Extradition Portal to speed up efforts to bring back fugitives. He directed state police to form teams to work with central agencies so they can prepare and follow up on extradition requests quickly. For decades, India’s counter-terrorism efforts relied on separate laws, agencies, and practices that developed over time. In 2026, PRAHAAR brought these elements together as the country’s first unified National Counter-Terrorism Policy and Strategy. Shah has stressed that the policy needs regular updates, should become part of daily operations, and must be implemented at every police station. The doctrine is built on seven main pillars. Prevention relies on intelligence to stop plots, propaganda, sleeper cells, funding, and arms networks before attacks happen. Response means local police act quickly and appropriately, with fast backup from central forces to avoid delays in the crucial first hours. Aggregating Internal Capacities means updating state police, standardising training, and working closely with agencies like the Multi-Agency Centre, the National Investigation Agency, the National Security Guard, and the Central Armed Police Forces. It also stresses the importance of human rights and the rule of law to keep counter-terrorism efforts legal and trustworthy. Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism focuses on de-radicalisation, involving communities, and supporting youth and women in at-risk areas to lower recruitment. Aligning International Efforts covers sharing intelligence, legal help, extradition, and diplomacy to stop terrorists from finding safe havens, weapons, or funding abroad. articles.title: Sense India Inaugurates India's First Sensory Tunnel for Persons with Deafblindness at ...
articles.content: Sense India Inaugurates India’s First Sensory Tunnel for Persons with Deafblindness at Sparsh Centre, Thane Naman Bansal September 29, 2026 PR – New sensory space at Sparsh Centre, CSR support of Shipping Corporation of India Lands and Assets Limited (SCILAL), creates pathways for children and young adults with deafblindness and multiple disabilities to explore, communicate and learn through touch, movement, sound and other senses Ahmedabad, 29 September 2026: Sense International India, an Ahmedabad based organisation working for people with deafblindness, today inaugurated India’s first Sensory Tunnel for persons with deafblindness and multiple disabilities at its Sparsh Centre in Thane, Maharashtra. Through this initiative, Sense India is introducing a dedicated sensory environment designed specifically to create new pathways for children and young adults with deafblindness and multiple disabilities to explore, communicate, learn and engage with the world around them through their senses. Supported through the CSR contribution of Shipping Corporation of India Lands and Assets Limited (SCILAL), the Sensory Tunnel is a purpose built, accessible environment designed to help children and young adults with deafblindness and multiple disabilities experience, explore and make sense of the world around them through structured sensory activities. The Sensory Tunnel features five specialised sensory zones: vision, tactile, vestibular (movement and balance), proprioceptive (body awareness) and auditory, where olfactory materials are incorporated for additional sensory exploration. Each zone offers carefully selected activities that encourage children to discover different textures, movements, sounds, patterns and sensations. Educators and therapists guide each individual through the space, introducing activities selectively and observing their responses to ensure that sensory experiences remain meaningful, comfortable and purposeful. Speaking at the inauguration, Uttam Kumar, CEO, Sense International India, said, “The Sensory Tunnel is more than a new facility. It represents a shift in how we think about inclusion by creating environments around the way persons with deafblindness and multiple disabilities actually experience and understand the world. For a child who may not be able to rely on sight or hearing in the way most of us do, touch, movement, body awareness, sound and smell can become powerful pathways to communication, learning and connection. The Sensory Tunnel gives children the opportunity to explore these pathways in a safe, structured and supportive environment. We are deeply grateful to the Shipping Corporation of India Lands and Assets Limited (SCILAL), for making this resource possible. Their support demonstrates how meaningful CSR partnerships can translate into spaces, opportunities and experiences that have a lasting impact on the lives of persons with deafblindness and multiple disabilities. We hope this Sensory Tunnel will not only benefit the children at Sparsh Centre every day, but also inspire greater understanding of what inclusive environments can look like.” Sparsh Centre, Sense India’s dedicated facility for persons with deafblindness and multiple disabilities in Thane, has been serving children and young adults in the district since 2022. The centre provides education, therapy, communication support and vocational training, working closely with families to build greater independence and participation. Six editions have been conducted so far, featuring leaders and practitioners discussing the impact of AI and digital transformation across their sectors. By Telangana Today Published Date - 29 September 2026, 05:54 PM AlgoShack , the Bengaluru-headquartered AI Native enterprise technology company behind algoQA, is bringing together leaders from banking, healthcare, retail, software engineering and Quality Engineering through its monthly Fireside Chat Series to discuss how enterprises can adopt AI while maintaining quality, trust and reliability. Launched in April 2026, the hybrid series is hosted at AlgoShack’s Bengaluru office and is also streamed for an online audience. Six editions have been conducted so far, featuring leaders and practitioners discussing the impact of AI and digital transformation across their sectors. The series began with a discussion on retail engineering and the growing complexity behind digital commerce platforms. The session explored how engineering and software quality teams are responding as digital experiences become more complex while customer expectations around speed and reliability continue to rise. The second edition focused on banking and financial services, bringing together a senior banking executive and founders from the credit-technology space. The discussion examined the balance between AI-led innovation and the governance, compliance and customer trust requirements that remain central to financial services. Healthcare was the focus of the following editions. One session brought together a radiologist and a health-technology engineer to discuss AI in medical imaging, including the importance of validation and clinical oversight when AI-enabled tools are used in diagnostic workflows. Another widened the discussion to digital transformation in healthcare, examining process redesign and collaboration between technology and clinical teams. The fifth edition focused on AI-accelerated software development and its implications for Quality Engineering. Enterprise software and quality leaders discussed how faster code generation is changing testing requirements and why release confidence remains important as AI takes on a greater role in software development. The sixth edition turned to the services industry and examined how Quality Engineering is evolving in the age of Agentic AI. The discussion reflected a shared view that Autonomous QE is still developing rather than representing a finished operating model. Panelists spoke about organisations moving from pilots toward broader adoption, while emphasising that human judgement and domain expertise remain important for edge cases, business context and end-to-end user experience. Across the six editions, the Fireside Chat Series has addressed a common challenge from different industry perspectives: how organisations can take advantage of AI-led speed and automation while maintaining confidence in the systems and outcomes they deliver. articles.title: Neeru Dhanda Scripts History, Wins India's First Asian Games Women's Trap Gold
articles.content: Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp Aichi-Nagoya, Sept 29: Neeru Dhanda scripted history at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Tuesday, becoming the first Indian woman to win an individual trap gold at the Asian Games after holding her nerve in a tense final and finishing with an Asian record-equalling score. Neeru, who had earlier won silver in the women’s team trap event, produced a superb comeback in the individual final to finish with 28 hits and add a historic gold to her medal tally. She began the eight-shooter final with a perfect five from five but slipped to third after missing her fourth shot in the second series. She responded immediately with a flawless series to move back into joint first before taking sole control as her rivals began to falter. With the medal positions tightening, Neeru delivered under pressure, hitting four of her first four targets in the final series to assure herself of at least silver before striking the decisive final target to finish on 28. The performance earned her gold and equalled the Asian record. Kuwait’s Hajar Abdulmalik took bronze after finishing level on 21 with China’s Sun Yunong, while Qatar’s Ray Bassil finished fourth. Neeru had entered the final as the top qualifier after scoring 118 before defeating Bassil in a shoot-off to secure pole position. The historic triumph capped a remarkable day for Neeru, who earlier teamed up with Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer to win silver in the women’s team trap event. The Indian trio finished with 328 hits, behind champions China with 346, while Kuwait took bronze with 325. Neeru’s gold was India’s fifth at the Aichi-Nagoya Games and added another landmark to the country’s shooting campaign. (Agencies)

articles.title: Who is Neeru Dhanda, India's first individual Asian Games gold medallist in women's trap
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | News | Who Is Neeru Dhanda Indias First Individual Asian Games Gold Medallist In Womens Trap Who is Neeru Dhanda, India’s first individual Asian Games gold medallist in women’s trap Indian shooter Neeru Dhanda won gold in women’s trap at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, becoming the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games trap medal. She scored 28 hits, setting an Asian record and securing India’s landmark victory By IANS Published Date - 29 September 2026, 12:17 PM Nagoya: For Neeru Dhanda, the road to Asian Games gold has been built one target at a time. On Tuesday, the 26-year-old Indian shooter finally had a medal around her neck that had eluded every Indian female trap shooter before her. Neeru produced a commanding performance in the women’s trap individual final in Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 28 hits to win gold and set a new Asian record. China’s Sun Yunong claimed silver with 26, while Kuwait’s Hajar Abdulmalik took bronze on 21. Neeru, who trains at Dr KSSR in New Delhi and is part of the Indian Army Marksmanship Unit as a Naib Subedar, first represented India at the 2022 ISSF World Championship in Osijek. Since then, she has established herself as a regular contender on the international circuit. She won the women’s trap title at the 2025 Asian Shooting Championship before producing the biggest breakthrough of her career earlier this year. At the ISSF Shotgun World Cup in Lonato, Italy, Neeru became the first Indian woman to win an individual World Cup gold in women’s trap. She also earned a mixed-team bronze at the World Cup in Almaty. The Asiad result marked the first time an Indian woman had won an Asian Games medal in the individual trap event. It also added another milestone to a year that has already transformed Neeru’s standing in international shooting. Her final was a lesson in recovering from setbacks without allowing them to grow. After a clean opening run, Neeru missed once in her second series and briefly slipped behind Sun and Abdulmalik. Instead of letting the error disrupt her rhythm, she responded with two successive perfect series. At the halfway stage, she had struck 19 of 20 targets and opened a two-hit advantage over her nearest challengers. By the time she reached the final five shots, the gold was firmly within her grasp. Neeru kept her composure to finish on 28 and complete a performance that had been in her control for much of the contest. The victory is the latest landmark in a rapid rise for the shooter from Jind, Haryana. Her Asian Games triumph carries another personal connection. Neeru took up shooting after being inspired by her cousin Lakshay Sheoran, who won silver in men’s trap at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta. Seven years later, she has gone one better. articles.title: India wins gold in shooting; Neeru Dhanda bags India's first individual gold in Asian Games
articles.content: NAGOYA: India won gold medal in the women's trap shooting event at the Asian Games, with Neeru Dhanda securing the top spot. This was India's first individual gold medal at the Asian Games and its fifth gold medal overall. Neeru finished first with 28 points, while China's Sun Yunong won silver with 26 points. Kuwait's Hajar Abdulmalik claimed the bronze medal. India also won silver in the women's shooting trap team event, finishing second with 328 points. China won gold in the women's team event, while Kuwait secured bronze. Meantime, Indian athletes continued to shine at the Asian Games yesterday, winning silver and bronze medals in track and field events. India secured three silver and three bronze medals in athletics alone. The country also added a silver medal in shooting and a bronze in Kurash. Malayali long jumper M Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh in the 1,500 metres, and Yashveer Singh in the javelin throw won silver medals in athletics. Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5,000 metres, while Vidhya Ramraj secured bronze in the 400-metre hurdles. Rohit Yadav won bronze in the men's javelin throw. In shooting, Esha Singh won silver in the 25-metre pistol event. Pinki Balhara claimed the bronze medal in Kurash. India wins gold in shooting; Neeru Dhanda bags India’s first individual gold in Asian Games

articles.title: Hyderabad-based TakeMe2Space to launch India's first orbital computing satellite on ...
articles.content: Home Trending News Startup News Hyderabad-based TakeMe2Space to launch India’s first orbital computing satellite on SpaceX Falcon 9 Hyderabad-based TakeMe2Space to launch India’s first orbital computing satellite on SpaceX Falcon 9 TakeMe2Space will fly India’s first networked orbital data centre mission on a SpaceX Falcon 9, plans to build a constellation of 6 satellites. By Ishita Ganguly 28 Sep 2026 Follow Us New Update TakeMe2Space to launch India’s first orbital computing satellite on SpaceX rocket Hyderabad-based spacetech startup TakeMe2Space will fly India’s first networked orbital data centre mission on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in 2028. TakeMe2Space to launch India’s first orbital computing satellite on SpaceX rocket The 2023-founded company, focused on building India ’s first orbital data centres, plans to build a constellation of six satellites over the next few years. Its MOI-1A spacecraft, a sub-50 kg satellite carrying Nvidia Orin NX edge-computing processors, is scheduled to fly on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission. Advertisment Add Startup Pedia As A Trusted Source TakeMe2Space will fly two 100-kilogram (kg) MOI (My Orbital Infrastructure) constellation satellites on a Falcon 9 as part of the Waymaker 2 rideshare mission. It has a launch window in late 2028, under a launch service agreement signed with RIDE! space, the launch mission management company that secured the slot. “Everything we have flown so far has been about proving that compute belongs in orbit. These two satellites are about proving it at a scale that pays. One and a half kilowatt (kW) of power, a 1-metre imager and a laser link between spacecraft are the smallest unit of an orbital data centre that actually behaves like one,” said Ronak Kumar Samantray, founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of TakeMe2Space. US-based Starcloud flew the first Nvidia Hopper 100 graphics processing unit (H100 GPU) in space in November 2025. It has since raised $170 million, while Google has said it will fly prototype Project Suncatcher satellites with Planet Labs by early 2027. Waymaker 2 will test whether two spacecraft can behave as one computer. TakeMe2Space’s first mission, MOI-TD (Technology Demonstrator), was launched on December 30, 2024, and ran more than 20 experiments in low Earth orbit. MOI-1 was lost in the PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle)-C62 launch failure in January 2026. “TakeMe2Space is bringing a new class of payload to rideshare, one that is defined by what it computes rather than what it carries. Getting two 100-kg spacecraft with laser links and 1.5 kW of power onto Waymaker 2 on schedule is exactly the kind of mission our platform exists for,” said Valentin Benoit, CEO of RIDE! space. The two spacecraft are the startup's first data centre-class satellites, following MOI-1a, which is scheduled to launch on October 1 on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission, with orbital injection expected by October 8 via a D-Orbit orbital transfer vehicle and launch and early orbit phase operations targeted for completion by October 16, and MOI-1b, which is also scheduled to launch in 2026.
